nodes.label: Meter — Autonomous Inference Treasurer
nodes.rationale: Differentiator: predictive scaling + autonomous procurement — existing tools show the graph, Meter acts on it because it can spend money under a pre-approved mandate.

nodes.label: Keep CONTEXT.md current policy
nodes.rationale: New sessions from different teammates/AI tools must open CONTEXT.md and immediately know where the project stands; update in the same turn as any decision.

nodes.label: Plain-assert self-check suites
nodes.rationale: test_proxy.py (~207 checks), test_predictor.py (~108), test_alerts.py (46) are plain asserts — no pytest, no fixtures; run the matching suite before committing.

nodes.label: Proxy (FastAPI hot path)
nodes.rationale: In the request path and must be boring: <5ms p50, no LLM, no network calls except to the provider, no synchronous Postgres write on the critical path. Auth → attribute → estimate → breaker → reserve → forward → capture.

nodes.label: Ledger (Postgres + Redis)
nodes.rationale: Postgres side (priced, attributed history) is the moat; Redis side (balances, reservations, breaker state, cached ceilings) is what makes enforcement fast enough to sit in front of production. SQLite in Phase 1, column names matching so the port is a schema swap.

nodes.label: Analyst Agent
nodes.rationale: Runs offline over the ledger on a schedule; detects retry loops, duplicate prompts, cache candidates, over-provisioned models; writes optimization plans with dollar estimates. This is where an LLM earns its place.

nodes.label: Treasurer Agent
nodes.rationale: Watches burn, projects time-to-zero, holds Prava mandates, executes top-ups. Heavily rate-limited; every decision logged with its inputs and thresholds.

nodes.label: Request lifecycle
nodes.rationale: AUTHENTICATE → ATTRIBUTE → ESTIMATE → RESERVE → BREAKER CHECK → FORWARD → CAPTURE; steps 1–5 must finish in single-digit milliseconds, capture is asynchronous after the client has its bytes.

nodes.label: The estimator — one design, not two
nodes.rationale: tiktoken counts input exactly (prompt is in hand); task-classification heuristic predicts output (response does not exist — irreducibly a prediction); trailing p95 for (project, endpoint, model) is the cold-start fallback. Feedback loop compares predicted vs actual and stores the variance so accuracy is a quotable number.

nodes.label: Authorize/capture pattern
nodes.rationale: A naive check-balance-then-call is wrong under concurrency — a thousand simultaneous requests all read the same healthy balance. Reserving up front makes the ceiling actually hold; deliberately the same primitive the payments world uses.

nodes.label: Serialization, not Redis
nodes.rationale: What makes authorize/capture correct is serialization, not Redis. With a single proxy process an in-process asyncio.Lock around the read-modify-write is an identical guarantee; Redis Lua becomes load-bearing only at replica #2. (PROPOSALS.md A5)

nodes.label: Reservation TTL heartbeat extension
nodes.rationale: Short TTL (120s) so a crashed worker releases holds, but SSE streams run minutes — a fixed TTL expires mid-flight on exactly the longest calls and fails silently. Stream loop re-EXPIREs roughly every 30s; keep TTL short and extend, do not just raise it.

nodes.label: Proxy as stream parser
nodes.rationale: The proxy is not a passthrough — it is a stream parser that happens to forward bytes. Gzip must be decompressed before parsing/forwarding; drop only a usage chunk that contains nothing else; capture must be scheduled before the first await in teardown or a client disconnect cancels it. Single most underestimated part of the build.

nodes.label: Versioned pricing files
nodes.rationale: Rates live in pricing/{version}.yaml, not code; each ledger row stores pricing_version so historical rows stay reproducible. Never edit an existing pricing file — add a new dated one, or every historical row silently reprices.

nodes.label: Ledger data model
nodes.rationale: Tables: projects, meter_keys, requests, annotations, wallets, mandates, treasury_events, breaker_events. prompt_hash makes cache-candidate/dedup a single query; trace_id makes cost-per-outcome possible. The interesting join is requests × annotations on trace_id — dollars per resolved ticket, a margin metric.

nodes.label: prompt_hash normalization
nodes.rationale: What goes into the hash is part of the schema: model in, system prompt in, message text in (whitespace-collapsed), image blocks out, and sampling parameters out — a retry storm re-sends identical prompts with jittered temperature, so including them would break retry-loop detection in the exact scenario it exists for.

nodes.label: meter.yaml budget file
nodes.rationale: Daily spend ceilings declared in meter.yaml in the repo so a limit changes by pull request; no file means no ceilings. Loader parses at boot and rebuilds projects/feature_budgets tables as an indexed local read cache.

nodes.label: Budget-as-code
nodes.rationale: meter.yaml wins; the loader replaces rather than upserts (a deleted ceiling must stop being enforced), rejects a config where any single feature ceiling exceeds its project's, and warns (does not reject) when feature ceilings sum past the project total — over-allocation is legal because both ceilings are checked independently at authorize time.

nodes.label: Treasurer loop (30s, write-ahead)
nodes.rationale: Every 30s: compute burn over trailing 1h, runway = balance/burn; if below topup_when_hours_remaining, check mandate scope, per-txn cap, rolling 24h cap, cooldown — all four in order — INSERT treasury_events (status=pending) write-ahead, call Prava with idempotency_key = that row's id, then update status and credit wallet. Persisting before calling is what makes the idempotency key stable across a retry; a top-up that double-charges ends any conversation about autonomous payments.

nodes.label: Circuit breaker (floor + burst)
nodes.rationale: Two conditions, both must hold: floor (trailing 5-min spend clears $20 — fast detection, 12x of nothing is still nothing) and burst (5-min rate exceeds trailing 1h average rate by 3x — stops an expensive-but-steady feature from tripping forever). Ratio bounded at 12x by window sizes; 0 disables burst. Modes: throttle (429, tag-scoped) vs revoke (403, key cut). Auto half-open after cooldown plus manual reset, or the demo strands on stage.

nodes.label: Google SRE Workbook multi-window alerting
nodes.source_location: §6 Why not the textbook multi-window alert
nodes.rationale: Cited prior art for the detection tension. Ported literally as two absolute thresholds it is wrong for a breaker: MWMBR pages humans about SLO burn where an hour of delay is fine, but catastrophic for a leaked API key. Meter uses the long window as a rate baseline instead of a second absolute threshold.

nodes.label: Fail-open policy
nodes.rationale: A cost tool that takes down production is not a cost tool. Datastore outage → serve against cached ceiling and reconcile. But authentication never fails open (unattributable calls are unbounded spend against someone else's key → 503), and revocation therefore fails closed by construction — a cut credential stays cut.

nodes.label: Revocation fails closed
nodes.source_location: §7 Where fail-open and the circuit breaker disagree
nodes.rationale: revoked_at is read during authentication; the revocation check consults that already-resolved record rather than issuing its own query, so there is no datastore call in the revocation path that could fail open. This is the half of the breaker that matters most during an incident, and the half that survives one.

nodes.label: Self-host is the product
nodes.rationale: No serious company routes production provider keys through a weekend-old startup's servers — keys stay in the customer's VPC; Meter is the control plane, not a key custodian. Hosted is the demo (needs long-lived connection support for SSE). Publish the overhead number: 'We add 3ms at p50'.

nodes.label: Lock-in mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Four mechanisms: critical path (removing Meter is a migration, hence fail-open default), ledger accrual (only priced, attributed history — does not port), budget-as-code (inside the customer's review process), mandate custody (system of record with authority). Features are copyable, position is not.

nodes.label: Prava (payment rail)
nodes.rationale: External payment provider the Treasurer agent calls to top up provider credits; mandate-scoped charges with idempotency keys; sandbox used for the demo.

nodes.label: Agentic Commerce Hackathon by Prava
nodes.rationale: 48-hour hackathon, 4-person team, tracks: Prava (Agentic Commerce) + Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) + Localhost (Startup Readiness) + Linq/Poke (iMessage alerts). Core requirement: the agent must complete a transaction using Prava.

nodes.label: MVP scope (Predictive Prava Top-up + Circuit Breaker)
nodes.rationale: MUST BUILD: FastAPI proxy, tiktoken prediction, Postgres/SQLite ledger, Prava sandbox, Mock Provider Billing, Treasurer loop, Circuit Breaker, Next.js dashboard, Poke alerts. FAKE/SIMULATE: mock provider billing (cannot really top up OpenAI with a Prava test card). REAL: forward requests to real OpenAI/Anthropic for training data.

nodes.label: Mock Provider Billing endpoint
nodes.rationale: POST /mock-openai/billing simulates OpenAI's billing system, accepting the Prava sandbox card and crediting the wallet — the one simulated component; everything on the Prava side of it is real. Say so in the demo.

nodes.label: Team roles
nodes.rationale: Shubh (proxy & infra), Shivam (payments & agent), Ammar (predictive AI), Tanay (frontend & DX). Four components, one process, one SQLite file.

nodes.label: Predictive Engine v2
nodes.rationale: predict() returns two numbers: predicted_* (forecast) and bound_* (what the call cannot exceed — exact when max_tokens set, making the ceiling guarantee structural). Exact tiktoken input counting including chat framing; raises on Claude rather than approximating with the wrong vocabulary. v1 regressed output on input length (R²=0.009) and was abandoned on evidence; v2 reads requested scope. Constants are parameters, not literals, so per-bucket fitting activates from ledger traffic.

nodes.label: Prediction deliberately biased high
nodes.rationale: Accuracy is asymmetric: under-predicting lets a request through that should have been blocked (ceiling silently fails); over-predicting holds budget released seconds later at CAPTURE. SAFETY_MARGIN = 1.15 aims high; under_prediction_rate tracked as first-class metric. The predictor never affects billing — only answers 'do we have room for this request?'

nodes.label: PreflightLLMCost evaluation (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated as a ready-made predictive engine; rejected — non-deterministic (Gaussian noise, ~70% spread on identical prompt, disqualifying for a reservation), its Tier 3 analysis is a formula over string length, its learning loop never connected, and only ~35 of 1,726 lines survive the fixes. Adopted its bucket taxonomy and starting ratios as cold-start priors; credits given in predictor/buckets.py.

nodes.label: Cross-model analysis
nodes.rationale: Compares which model is more token-efficient per task using actual usage returned by each provider — deliberately does not depend on the predictor (which is OpenAI-only). Runs as an offline script over a fixed prompt suite, not shadow-calling in the request path: doubling the customer's bill inside a cost-control tool would be noticed (PROPOSALS.md B11).

nodes.label: Dashboard (Next.js 16)
nodes.rationale: Reads meter.db directly and read-only; every query guards on the table existing (checks sqlite_master) so a half-built database shows what it has instead of 500ing. Mission-control darkroom visual system; status colors chosen against the colorblind case (ΔE 10.6 ramp). Team Budget card mirrors proxy/budget.py's rolling window and meter.yaml order.

nodes.label: Alerts (Poke/Linq iMessage)
nodes.rationale: POST /v3/messages on the Linq Partner API resolves sending line and chat itself. Dispatched on a daemon thread, never awaited — an inline HTTP call would put a third party's latency in front of production traffic; swallows every exception. Per-scope cooldown (default 300s) so a re-tripping breaker does not mute the channel. Destination validation is NANP-aware, not just E.164.

nodes.label: 90-second demo narrative
nodes.rationale: The Predictive Prava Save: 3am batch job predicted at $14.50 against a $4.00 OpenAI balance → Treasurer Agent wakes up, calls Prava, tops up autonomously, zero dropped requests. Closed with the leaked-key Poke alert beat.

nodes.label: Standing mandate over one-time card
nodes.rationale: §4/§5B and the pitch script still say 'one-time scoped card'; the mandate is strictly better for the Treasurer — the human approves once with a passkey, the agent charges repeatedly with none. Wording needs updating before the demo.

nodes.label: POST /v1/annotate (attribution rung 3)
nodes.rationale: Returns the trace's total cost, request count and margin, scoped to the calling key's project — a trace_id is caller-supplied, so without that scope any key could read another project's spend (project_id on annotations approved on security grounds). value_usd optional; absent → margin_usd null, because 'broke even' and 'we don't know the value' are different facts.

nodes.label: PROPOSALS.md
nodes.rationale: Staging area for contradictions between README/CONTEXT/ARCHITECTURE and gaps they leave undefined; items applied to the source-of-truth docs only after a human approves. 26 items: A1–A6 (contradictions), B1–B18 (gaps), C1–C4 (verification).

nodes.label: A1 — Breaker detection: floor + burst
nodes.rationale: CONTEXT §5C and PLAN said flat $20/5min; ARCHITECTURE §6 said a ratio vs 7-day baseline. Shipped detection satisfies both: absolute floor AND burst ratio vs trailing-hour average (3x default). Keeps both source documents true rather than picking a winner.

nodes.label: A5 — No Redis in the 48-hour build
nodes.rationale: Redis is not what makes authorize/capture correct — serialization is. In-process asyncio.Lock around the same read-modify-write gives an identical guarantee for one proxy process with none of the operational cost; Redis becomes load-bearing at replica #2 and the upgrade is one function. Prior art: LiteLLM runs FastAPI + Redis + Postgres at scale.

nodes.label: B17 — Feature-ceiling validation rule
nodes.rationale: Rejecting a project whose feature ceilings sum past its own inverts the failure mode — the response to 'over-allocated on paper' becomes no enforcement at all. Replaced with LiteLLM's actual rule: reject a single feature above its project, warn on the sibling sum. Both ceilings are checked independently at authorize time.

nodes.label: B18 — Treasury control plane auth
nodes.rationale: Every /v1 route authenticated but none of the treasury surface did; verified live: an unauthenticated POST /charge reached the Prava sandbox (Prava's own AUTH_1001 rejected it). Money-moving routes now require a Meter key via a _authed_key dependency; read-only and demo routes stay open.

nodes.label: C1 — Pricing rates verified
nodes.rationale: First draft written from memory was wrong in both directions (Haiku 4.5 under-priced 20%, opus entry 3x high). Claude Sonnet 5 intro pricing ($2/$10 per MTok) expires 2026-08-31 → create pricing/2026-09-01.yaml then; never edit the existing file or every historical row silently reprices.

nodes.label: LiteLLM (prior art)
nodes.rationale: Closest open-source equivalent to Meter; enforces budgets hierarchically (key → user → team → org, child cannot exceed parent) — the shape Meter's project → feature nesting mirrors. Also runs FastAPI + Redis + Postgres, agreeing with ARCHITECTURE.md at scale.

nodes.label: Attribution ladder (rungs 0–3)
nodes.rationale: Rung 0 base URL swap (project/environment/model/endpoint); rung 1 X-Meter-Feature/-Actor; rung 2 X-Meter-Trace (cost per workflow); rung 3 POST /v1/annotate (cost per outcome — turns a cost tool into a margin tool). Each rung costs a little more integration, buys a lot more resolution.

nodes.label: compose.yaml
nodes.rationale: The whole backend — proxy, treasury, mock provider — is one process, so one service; named volume for the ledger; meter.yaml and pricing/ mounted read-only so budget-as-code and pricing change by PR, not by exec.

nodes.label: Prava — payment stack for agentic checkout
nodes.rationale: Turns a user's permission into a one-time, merchant-scoped card credential — a programmable payment proxy. Decouples the agent's ability to buy from the user's sensitive data; zero PCI scope.

nodes.label: Prava session
nodes.rationale: The workspace for one payment; session_token authenticates subsequent operations, short-lived, single-use, revocable.

nodes.label: Prava passkey
nodes.rationale: The user's biometric approval (Touch ID / Face ID) that grants a permission; FIDO standard behind passkeys.

nodes.label: Prava mandate
nodes.rationale: The resulting permission after passkey approval: this merchant, up to this amount, for this long. Standing spend authorization — approve once, let an agent charge later within caps. Charge a Mandate mints single-use card credentials with no passkey.

nodes.label: Prava payment token
nodes.rationale: The single-use card credential issued against a mandate.

nodes.label: Prava dual-key system
nodes.rationale: Merchant secret key (sk_test_*/sk_live_*, Bearer, backend only) and publishable key (pk_test_*/pk_live_*, SDK init, frontend-safe). Never expose secret keys client-side or in logs.

nodes.label: Prava sandbox / production environments
nodes.rationale: Sandbox: sk_test_* against sandbox.api.prava.space, self-serve. Production: sk_live_* against api.prava.space, requires verification. Environment pairing is a common AUTH_1001 cause.

nodes.label: Prava integration paths (Embedded / Hosted / Agent)
nodes.rationale: Payment is always AI/agent-mediated; what differs is who owns the interface and where the card UI lives. Agent path (Prava Pay via MCP or CLI) is for AI-agent-owned interfaces like OpenClaw, Hermes, ChatGPT.
